**Co‑development & Co‑commercialization of a single Phase 3 oncology asset (US biotech – EU pharma)** | Item | Key Point | |------|-----------| | **Asset** | Pre‑revenue biotech; one Phase 3 oncology drug (FDA accelerated‑approval possible) | | **Partner** | EU‑based pharma with strong commercial platform in Europe/UK | | **Territorial split** | US – biotech; EU/UK – pharma | | **Deal type** | Upfront + milestone payments + tiered royalty (cross‑licensing on sales outside each party’s territory) | Below is a step‑by‑step walk‑through that incorporates realistic probabilities, market data and industry practice. --- ## 1. Valuation Analysis ### 1.1 rNPV – Risk‑Adjusted Net Present Value | Step | Description | |------|-------------| | **A. Cash‑flow forecast** | • US: $70 k/patient‑year × 10 % of the 30 M‑patient market → ~$210 M first year, growing 5 %/yr for 10 yrs.
• EU/UK: €60 k/patient‑year × 8 % of the 20 M‑patient market → ~$96 M first year, 4 %/yr growth. | | **B. Probability weighting** | • Phase 3 success (P₃) = 35 % (industry average for a single oncology asset).
• FDA accelerated approval probability (P_A) = 55 % conditional on P₃.
• EMA/MHRA approval probability (P_EU) = 72 % conditional on P₃. | | **C. Discount rate** | • Cost of capital ≈ 8 %.
• Risk premium for a pre‑revenue biotech ≈ 4–7 % → total 12–15 %. | | **D. Weighted cash flows** | Multiply each year’s forecast by cumulative probability (e.g., Year 1 sales × P₃ × P_A × P_EU). Discount at 13 %. | ### 1.2 Sensitivity & Scenario Analysis | Scenario | rNPV (USD) | |----------|------------| | **Best‑case** (high uptake, accelerated approval in both regions) | ≈ $1.8 bn | | **Base‑case** (standard Phase 3 success, no accelerated approval) | ≈ $1.2 bn | | **Worst‑case** (failure to meet endpoints or regulatory rejection) | $0 | *These ranges guide the upside that can be captured in upfront/milestone/royalty terms.* --- ## 2. Deal Structure ### 2.1 Payment Components | Component | Typical Value (USD) | Rationale | |-----------|--------------------|-----------| | **Upfront** | $35–$70 M | Covers early‑stage development costs; reflects pre‑revenue status and the fact that the biotech retains US commercial rights. | | **Milestones** | $30–$60 M each (see table below) | Tiered by regulatory & commercial events; weighted by probability of success. | | **Royalty (cross‑licensing)** | • **US** – pharma pays 12 % on biotech’s US sales.
• **EU/UK** – biotech pays 14 % on pharma’s EU/UK sales. | Licensee pays higher rate; tiered to reward early revenue growth. | | **Territorial split** | Biotech: US; Pharma: EU/UK | Matches each party’s commercial strengths and reduces overlap. | ### 2.2 Milestone Calibration | Milestone | Typical Amount | Probability Weight | Rationale | |-----------|----------------|--------------------|-----------| | **IND filing (US)** | $10–$15 M | 100 % | Early commitment to development. | | **Phase 3 initiation** | $30–$40 M | 35 % (P₃) | Reflects Phase 3 success probability. | | **FDA approval (full or accelerated)** | $50–$60 M | 55 % of P₃ | Captures upside from accelerated pathway. | | **EMA/MHRA approval** | $35–$45 M | 72 % of P₃ | Separate regulatory risk in EU/UK. | | **First commercial sales (US)** | $40–$50 M | 35 % of P₃ | Aligns with launch timing. | | **First commercial sales (EU/UK)** | $30–$40 M | 72 % of P₃ | Reflects stronger sales pipeline in Europe. | *The present value of all milestones is designed to equal ≈ 70–80 % of the rNPV, ensuring that the biotech’s upside is captured while keeping the pharma’s risk‑adjusted return attractive.* ### 2.3 Royalty Structure (Cross‑Licensing) | Territory | Licensee | Royalty Rate | Tier | |-----------|----------|--------------|------| | **US** | Pharma | 12 % on US sales | 10 % for first $200 M, 8 % thereafter | | **EU/UK** | Biotech | 14 % on EU/UK sales | 12 % for first €150 M, 10 % thereafter | *The higher rate paid by the licensee reflects standard industry practice.* ### 2.4 Payment Timing | Payment | Trigger | Typical Window | |---------|---------|----------------| | Upfront | Signing | Net of cash within 30 days | | IND filing | Within 60 days | – | | Phase 3 initiation | First patient enrolled | – | | FDA approval | Submission & acceptance | – | | EMA/MHRA approval | Submission & acceptance | – | | Commercial sales | Quarterly | Minimum guarantee for first year | --- ## 3. Risk‑Sharing Framework ### 3.1 Clinical‑Program Risk | Party | Responsibility | Mitigation | |-------|-----------------|------------| | **Biotech** | Early‑phase data generation (Phase 1/2), IND filing, Phase 3 study design & execution. | Upfront + milestone payments cover costs; milestone tied to patient enrollment. | | **Pharma** | Commercial launch in EU/UK, marketing, sales force, reimbursement negotiations. | Royalty structure aligns incentives; pharma bears commercial risk outside US. | ### 3.2 Regulatory Risk | Region | Primary Regulator | IP & Data Ownership | Risk Allocation | |--------|-------------------|---------------------|-----------------| | **US** | FDA (accelerated approval) | Biotech owns data; shares with pharma under NDA. | Both parties share FDA risk: biotech generates data, pharma files and manages post‑approval obligations. | | **EU/UK** | EMA / MHRA | Biotech retains core patents; licenses to pharma for EU/UK territories. | Pharma bears regulatory risk in Europe; biotech receives milestone upon approval. | ### 3.3 Intellectual Property Exposure | Asset | Ownership | Licensing | |-------|-----------|-----------| | **Core oncology patents** | Biotech | Exclusive license to pharma for EU/UK (territorial). | | **Secondary patents / formulations** | Pharma | Licenses to biotech for US territory. | | **Trade secrets / manufacturing process** | Shared under confidentiality agreement | Pharma may sublicense within its network. | *Indemnification clauses protect both parties from third‑party IP infringement claims.* ### 3.4 Commercial & Marketing Risk - **US (Biotech)** – Responsible for launch, pricing strategy, reimbursement negotiations, and sales force deployment. - **EU/UK (Pharma)** – Handles all commercial activities in its territories; responsible for market access, pricing, and distribution. *Both parties agree to share safety data and clinical outcomes but keep commercial performance data confidential.* ### 3.5 Exit & Termination Clauses | Scenario | Action | |----------|--------| | **Regulatory failure** | Biotech may terminate with return of upfront; pharma retains earned milestones. | | **Commercial underperformance** | After 2 years, either party can renegotiate royalty rates or consider a buy‑out option. | | **IP disputes** | Mediation first, then arbitration (ICC rules). | --- ## 4. Financial Structure & Deal Economics ### 4.1 Present Value of Payments to Biotech | Component | PV (USD) | % of rNPV | |-----------|----------|------------| | Upfront | $50 M | 4–6 % | | Milestones | $120–$150 M | 10–12 % | | Royalty Income (EU/UK, first 5 yrs) | $80–$100 M | 7–9 % | | **Total PV** | $250–$300 M | 20–25 % | *The biotech’s share is roughly a quarter of the rNPV, reflecting its early‑stage risk.* ### 4.2 Pharma’s Expected Cash Flow | Component | PV (USD) | % of rNPV | |-----------|----------|------------| | Royalty Income (US, first 5 yrs) | $70–$90 M | 6–8 % | | Net Sales after royalty | $400–$500 M | 35–40 % | | **Total PV** | $470–$590 M | 40–50 % | *Pharma’s larger share reflects its commercial leverage in Europe and the fact that it pays royalties on US sales.* ### 4.3 Sensitivity to Accelerated Approval - **If accelerated approval achieved (US)**: Upfront + milestone payments increase by ~5 %; royalty upside increases by ~3 %. - **If not**: Milestone amounts reduce by ~10 %; overall PV for biotech falls by ~15 %. ### 4.4 Currency & Tax Considerations | Issue | Mitigation | |-------|------------| | **Currency risk** | Hedge upfront and milestone payments in USD; use forward contracts for EU/UK royalties. | | **Withholding tax** | Structure royalty flows through a low‑tax jurisdiction (e.g., Ireland) with treaty benefits to reduce withholding on EU/UK royalties. | | **Taxation of milestones** | Treat as ordinary income in the payer’s jurisdiction; consider tax credits or deductions for R&D spend. | ### 4.5 Accounting & Reporting - **ASC 606** – Biotech recognizes royalty income when sales are recognized by pharma in its territory. - **Joint reporting** – Each party reports only its own revenue; safety data shared under a joint database agreement. --- ## 5. Recommendations for Negotiation 1. **Define Success Metrics Clearly** – Specify endpoints, sample size, and statistical thresholds that trigger each milestone. 2. **Align Incentives on Commercial Performance** – Include performance‑based royalty caps (e.g., “royalty floor” if sales fall below a threshold) to protect the biotech from extreme underperformance. 3. **Protect IP in Both Regions** – Draft robust IP assignment/licensing clauses; include indemnification for third‑party claims and clear ownership of data generated post‑approval. 4. **Escrow Only If Needed** – Use an escrow for milestone payments only if there is a genuine cash‑flow risk (e.g., biotech’s liquidity). Otherwise, standard payment terms suffice. 5. **Plan for Regulatory Changes** – Include provisions that allow adjustment of milestones or royalty rates if accelerated approval criteria change or orphan drug status is granted/denied. 6. **Joint Data & Safety Plan** – Agree on a shared safety database and joint pharmacovigilance responsibilities; keep commercial performance data confidential to each party’s territory. --- ### Bottom Line - The **rNPV** of the asset (≈ $1.2–1.8 bn) supports an upfront payment of **$35–70 M**, milestone payments totaling **$180–240 M**, and a tiered royalty structure that rewards early sales growth while protecting both parties’ interests. - The **territorial split** aligns each party’s commercial strengths with the appropriate risk profile: biotech retains US regulatory & commercial risk; pharma bears EU/UK regulatory & commercial risk. - A **risk‑sharing framework** that clearly delineates clinical, regulatory, IP and commercial responsibilities ensures that upside is captured while keeping downside exposure proportional to each party’s contribution. With these calibrated terms, the partnership can move forward with a fair valuation, balanced risk allocation and aligned incentives for both the US biotech and the EU pharma.
